root_cause: Three issues compound into the reported bugs: (1) src/invoice.js computes `taxFor(subtotal, region)` using the pre-discount subtotal instead of `subtotal - discount`, so discounted invoices are taxed on too much money; (2) src/money.js's `applyRate` uses `Math.floor(cents * rate)`, truncating instead of rounding half up, so any fractional-cent result (tax, and once added, percentage discounts) is systematically a cent too low; (3) src/discount.js/codes.js have no 'percent' discount type and `lookup()` does a case-sensitive key match, so SAVE10/SAVE25 don't exist and codes aren't case-insensitive.

changes.change: Change `applyRate` to round half up instead of truncating: `return Math.floor(cents * rate + 0.5);`. This single change fixes rounding for both tax (via taxFor) and the new percentage discounts, since both route through applyRate.
Add two percentage entries to CODES: `SAVE10: { type: 'percent', rate: 0.10 }` and `SAVE25: { type: 'percent', rate: 0.25 }`, alongside the existing fixed WELCOME5/LOYAL20 entries.

Import `applyRate` from './money'. In `lookup(code)`, match case-insensitively via `const entry = CODES[String(code).toUpperCase()];` (keep the thrown message as `Unknown discount code: ${code}` using the original input, so the existing 'unknown code throws' test keeps passing). In `discountFor`, add a branch `if (entry.type === 'percent') return Math.min(applyRate(subtotalCents, entry.rate), subtotalCents);` before the 'Unsupported code type' throw.

Compute discount first (unchanged), then compute tax on the post-discount amount: change `const tax = taxFor(subtotal, region);` to `const tax = taxFor(subtotal - discount, region);`. The `total = subtotal - discount + tax` formula is unchanged since discount/tax are now correctly ordered inputs.

test_cases.name: tax rounds half up instead of truncating (regression for 'one cent too low')
test_cases.expected: { subtotal: 200, discount: 0, tax: 13, total: 213 }  // 200 * 0.0625 = 12.5 -> rounds up to 13, not floored to 12

test_cases.name: fixed discount applied before tax (regression for 'overcharged on tax')
test_cases.call: buildInvoice([{ name: 'widget', price: 100.00, qty: 1 }], { region: 'CA', code: 'WELCOME5' })
test_cases.expected: { subtotal: 10000, discount: 500, tax: 689, total: 10189 }  // tax computed on 9500 (10000-500): 9500*0.0725=688.75 -> rounds to 689

test_cases.name: percentage discount SAVE10 reduces taxable base, with half-up rounding on tax
test_cases.call: buildInvoice([{ name: 'widget', price: 100.00, qty: 1 }], { region: 'CA', code: 'SAVE10' })

test_cases.name: percentage discount SAVE25 is case-insensitive (lowercase code), no tax region
test_cases.call: buildInvoice([{ name: 'gadget', price: 50.00, qty: 1 }], { region: 'OR', code: 'save25' })
test_cases.expected: { subtotal: 5000, discount: 1250, tax: 0, total: 3750 }  // 'save25' matches SAVE25 case-insensitively: 5000*0.25=1250

test_cases.name: fixed discount code is also case-insensitive (lowercase code)
test_cases.call: buildInvoice([{ name: 'book', price: 30.00, qty: 1 }], { region: 'OR', code: 'welcome5' })

test_cases.name: unknown discount code still throws (existing behavior preserved)
